property_summary: After any external call to withdrawReward completes, the rewardsForA mapping for the recipient must always be zero, which the reference enforces by resetting before the call and the bug violates by leaving it unchanged.

After getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) completes, the claimedBonus mapping for recipient must be true and rewardsForA must be zero; the bug leaves rewardsForA uncleared because withdrawReward no longer resets it, allowing double claims.

After getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) completes, the contract's balance must decrease by exactly 100; the bug allows withdrawing the 100 repeatedly without reducing the contract balance further because rewardsForA is never reset.

For any address that has not claimed a bonus, after a successful getFirstWithdrawalBonus, the contract's balance must decrease by exactly 100; in the buggy version, a re-entrant recipient can call withdrawReward again during the external call and receive a second full withdrawal, causing the balance to decrease by more than 100.

After a successful withdrawal via withdrawReward, the sum of the contract's balance and the total of all recorded rewardsForA must remain constant; the buggy version fails to reset rewardsForA, so a re-entrant call can withdraw the same reward twice and break this invariant.

After any call to withdrawReward, rewardsForA for the recipient must be zero in the correct contract; the buggy version leaves it non-zero when a reentrant callee re-enters via getFirstWithdrawalBonus before the reset.

After a call to withdrawReward(recipient) completes, the rewardsForA mapping for that recipient must be zero; the buggy version leaves it non-zero when a reentrant callee calls getFirstWithdrawalBonus before the reset, letting the attacker double-claim the bonus.

After any call to withdrawReward(recipient), the userBalances mapping for that recipient must remain zero because the contract never manipulates it, while the reentrancy bug allows a callee to call getFirstWithdrawalBonus and inflate rewardsForA before the reset, enabling a double-claim detectable by a non-zero userBalances after the call.

After withdrawReward completes for any recipient, the rewardsForA balance for that recipient must be zero; the buggy version leaves it non-zero when a malicious callee re-enters via getFirstWithdrawalBonus before the reset.

After any external call to withdrawReward(recipient), the contract's ETH balance must decrease by at least the amount withdrawn, which the buggy version violates when an attacker re-enters via getFirstWithdrawalBonus before the reset, causing the contract to send the reward twice (observable through balance difference).

After a successful getFirstWithdrawalBonus, the contract's balance must be at least the sum of userBalances and rewardsForA; the buggy version allows reentrancy that drains the contract, violating this invariant.

After a call to withdrawReward by a re-entrant attacker within getFirstWithdrawalBonus, the reference's _locked prevents re-enter while the mutant allows it; thus the mutant's _locked will be false (unlocked) after the call, while the reference's must remain false as well, but the re-entrant attack in the mutant causes an extra re-entry that leaves userBalances or rewardsForA zero while _locked is updated incorrectly, so the invariant that _locked is false after any public call completes holds for the reference but the mutant can leave _locked true or cause inconsistent state.

After a call to getFirstWithdrawalBonus that involves a re-entrant external call within withdrawReward, the reference contract's _locked correctly returns to false, while the mutant allows reentry and results in _locked being true.

After a self-reentrant call to getFirstWithdrawalBonus, the reference contract correctly reverts the second attempt, leaving claimedBonus[attacker] true and balance unchanged, while the mutant allows reentry, causing claimedBonus[attacker] to become false after the second call and double-spend the bonus, which can be observed by checking claimedBonus[attacker] after the first call completes.
After any successful getFirstWithdrawalBonus call, the contract's _locked state variable must be false; the mutant leaves it true due to reentrancy being allowed.

In the reference contract, a second call to withdrawReward succeeds because the lock is released after the first call; in the buggy contract, a second call to withdrawReward always reverts because the lock is never released.
After a successful call to withdrawReward, the _locked flag must be reset to false enabling further calls; the buggy modifier leaves _locked permanently true causing subsequent calls to revert.
After any successful withdrawal, the reentrancy lock (_locked) must return to false, allowing subsequent calls; the bug leaves it permanently true, blocking all further withdrawals.

After any successful non-reentrant call through withdrawReward, the lock _locked must be false, allowing at least one more non-reentrant call to succeed; the buggy modifier leaves _locked permanently true, so the second call always reverts.

After any call to withdrawReward completes, the reentrancy lock _locked must be false, allowing another non-reentrant call to succeed; the buggy modifier never resets _locked to false, so a subsequent call reverts.
For any address with a zero balance, getFirstWithdrawalBonus reverts only on the first call, not on the second.
getFirstWithdrawalBonus reverts on any call after the first for the same recipient.
For any address, getFirstWithdrawalBonus reverts if it has already been called successfully for that address.
getFirstWithdrawalBonus reverts if the recipient address has any non-zero Ether balance.
getFirstWithdrawalBonus reverts if and only if the recipient contract has a non-zero balance.

A single recipient must never be able to claim more than one first-withdrawal bonus; the correct contract limits total bonus withdrawals per address to exactly 100, whereas the buggy version allows multiple claims.

After any call to getFirstWithdrawalBonus, the claimedBonus flag for the recipient must be true; the buggy contract allows a call where claimedBonus remains false due to an internal revert occurring after the require is removed.

For any recipient, after a successful call to getFirstWithdrawalBonus, the contract's ETH balance must decrease by exactly 100 wei; the buggy version allows repeated calls that drain more than 100 wei from the contract.

The cumulative rewards recorded for any recipient must never exceed the total balance of the contract; the buggy version allows a recipient to claim multiple bonuses, causing rewards to exceed contract ETH.
A recipient's balance after getFirstWithdrawalBonus never exceeds the sum of their initial balance plus 100.
